hindi: कर्म से कोई उसे नहीं पाता, जिसने सदा बढ़ने वाले को बनाया है, यज्ञों से मानो, सब से स्तुत, बलवान, अजेय और बल से निर्भीक इन्द्र को।
english: No one reaches by deed him who has made [him] ever-growing, as it were through sacrifices: Indra, praised by all, mighty, unassailed, bold through strength.
notes: The construction is uncertain: na may be the negative of line 1 or the particle 'like' in line 2 (read here as 'as it were'); the object of cakāra is taken as Indra (sadāvṛdham agreeing with indram). kiṣṭam is read kiḥ + tam (na kiḥ, 'no one'). ṛbhvasam 'skilful, mighty' is uncertain.
lines_deva: न किष्टं कर्मणा नशद्यश्चकार सदावृधम्
इन्द्रं न यज्ञैर्विश्वगूर्तमृभ्वसमधृष्टं धृष्णुमोजसा
lines_iast: na kiṣṭaṃ karmaṇā naśadyaścakāra sadāvṛdham
indraṃ na yajñairviśvagūrtamṛbhvasamadhṛṣṭaṃ dhṛṣṇumojasā

hindi: वह जो बिना बन्धन के भी, कन्धे की हड्डियों के कटने से पहले, सन्धि को जोड़ने वाला है; वह धनवान मघवन् मुड़े हुए को फिर ठीक करने वाला है।
english: He who, even without bandage, before the piercing of the collar-bones, joins the joint, the bountiful one rich in wealth, who sets right again what is bent.
notes: Hard verse: jatrubhya ātṛdaḥ (collar-bones / ātṛd 'piercing, cutting') and abhiśriṣaḥ (binding, bandage) are rendered literally; the sense of the phrase is uncertain. Read as a description of Indra (maghavā). Only the literal meaning is given, no medical interpretation.
lines_deva: य ऋते चिदभिश्रिषः पुरा जत्रुभ्य आतृदः
सन्धाता सन्धिं मघवा पुरूवसुर्निष्कर्ता विह्रुतं पुनः
lines_iast: ya ṛte cidabhiśriṣaḥ purā jatrubhya ātṛdaḥ
sandhātā sandhiṃ maghavā purūvasurniṣkartā vihrutaṃ punaḥ

words.gloss: and (ā … ā 'a thousand and a hundred')

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सोम पीने के लिए सोने के रथ में जुते हुए, प्रार्थना से जोड़े गए, लम्बे केशों वाले एक हजार और एक सौ घोड़े तुम्हें यहाँ लाएँ।
english: May the long-maned bay horses, a thousand and a hundred, yoked to the golden chariot and harnessed by prayer, bring you here, O Indra, to drink the Soma.
notes: yuktā is read as yuktāḥ (Vedic nominative plural form). 'a thousand and a hundred' is the literal sense of sahasram ā śatam (a large number).
lines_deva: आ त्वा सहस्रमा शतं युक्ता रथे हिरण्यये
ब्रह्मयुजो हरय इन्द्र केशिनो वहन्तु सोमपीतये
lines_iast: ā tvā sahasramā śataṃ yuktā rathe hiraṇyaye
brahmayujo haraya indra keśino vahantu somapītaye

hindi: हे इन्द्र, आनन्द देने वाले, मोर के पंखों जैसे रोमों वाले घोड़ों के साथ आओ। कोई भी तुम्हें न रोके, जैसे जाल वाले रोकते हैं; उन्हें मरुभूमि की तरह पार कर जाओ।
english: Come, O Indra, with exhilarating bay horses with peacock-feather hair. Let none hold you back, like fowlers; go beyond them as over a desert.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda has 'ni yaman vim na pāśinaḥ' (as fowlers a bird); the Sāmaveda's 'yemur inna' may be a chant variant of this, so the word 'in' is uncertain

notes: 'yemur inna' is a Sāmaveda variant of the Rigveda 'yaman vim na'; the translation follows the RV sense ('as fowlers [hold] a bird'), the bird being understood. In words, inna is split in + na, with 'in' uncertain. Reviewer: the 'bird' of the Rigveda parallel is not rendered, because the printed Sāmaveda text has no word for it.
lines_deva: आ मन्द्रैरिन्द्र हरिभिर्याहि मयूररोमभिः
मा त्वा के चिन्नि येमुरिन्न पाशिनोऽति धन्वेव ताँ इहि
lines_iast: ā mandrairindra haribhiryāhi mayūraromabhiḥ
mā tvā ke cinni yemurinna pāśino'ti dhanveva tā~ ihi

hindi: तुम ही, देव होकर, हे सबसे बलवान, मनुष्य की प्रशंसा करते हो। हे मघवन्, तुमसे अन्य कोई दयालु नहीं है; हे इन्द्र, मैं तुमसे एक वचन कहता हूँ।
english: You indeed, being a god, O most mighty, praise the mortal. There is no one other than you, O bountiful one, who is gracious; O Indra, I speak a word to you.

text_flags.why: possible: ar for ṛ in a chant-orthography spelling; the word is mṛḍitā 'gracious one'

notes: pra śaṃsiṣaḥ is taken as 'praise, speak well of, favour'; the exact nuance is uncertain. 'marḍitā' read as mṛḍitā (agent noun of √mṛḍ, to be gracious).
lines_deva: त्वमङ्ग प्र शँसिषो देवः शविष्ठ मर्त्यम्
न त्वदन्यो मघवन्नस्ति मर्डितेन्द्र ब्रवीमि ते वचः
lines_iast: tvamaṅga pra śa~siṣo devaḥ śaviṣṭha martyam
na tvadanyo maghavannasti marḍitendra bravīmi te vacaḥ

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम यशस्वी, बलवान और बल के स्वामी हो। तुम अकेले ही शत्रुओं को बिना रोक-टोक मारते हो; बहुत अप्रेरित, प्रजाओं के धारक।
english: You, O Indra, are glorious, mighty, lord of strength. You alone slay the foes irresistibly, much unimpelled, supporter of the peoples.
notes: ṛjīṣin (rendered 'mighty one') and apratīni (taken as an adverb 'irresistibly'; possibly n. acc. pl. 'unopposed') are uncertain. puru anuttaḥ: 'purv anuttaḥ' by sandhi; read 'much / often, unimpelled'.
lines_deva: त्वमिन्द्र यशा अस्यृजीषी शवसस्पतिः
त्वं वृत्राणि हँस्यप्रतीन्येक इत्पुर्वनुत्तश्चर्षणीधृतिः
lines_iast: tvamindra yaśā asyṛjīṣī śavasaspatiḥ
tvaṃ vṛtrāṇi ha~syapratīnyeka itpurvanuttaścarṣaṇīdhṛtiḥ

words.gloss: for the worship of the gods

hindi: देवों की उपासना के लिए इन्द्र को ही बुलाते हैं, यज्ञ के चलते समय इन्द्र को; हम उत्सुक उपासक युद्ध में इन्द्र को बुलाते हैं, धन की प्राप्ति के लिए इन्द्र को।
english: We call Indra indeed for the worship of the gods; Indra, when the sacrifice proceeds; we, the eager ones, call Indra in battle; Indra for the winning of wealth.

text_flags.why: possible: the 1 pl. middle ending is -mahe; the final -a may be a chant variant or a typing slip

notes: 'we call' is supplied from havāmahe for the first three Indra phrases. vaninaḥ (here 'eager ones, suppliants') is uncertain.
lines_deva: इन्द्रमिद्देवतातय इन्द्रं प्रयत्यध्वरे
इन्द्रँ समीके वनिनो हवामह इन्द्रं धनस्य सातये
lines_iast: indramiddevatātaya indraṃ prayatyadhvare
indra~ samīke vanino havāmaha indraṃ dhanasya sātaye

hindi: हे बहुधन, मेरी ये वाणियाँ तुम्हें बढ़ाएँ। निर्मल रंग वाले, शुद्ध, ज्ञानियों ने स्तोत्रों से तुम्हारी स्तुति की है।
english: May these songs of mine strengthen you, O rich in wealth. The pure, bright-coloured, inspired ones have praised [you] with their hymns.
notes: The object of abhi anūṣata (you) is understood. pāvakavarṇāḥ may describe the singers or the songs; taken as the singers.
lines_deva: इमा उ त्वा पुरूवसो गिरो वर्धन्तु या मम
पावकवर्णाः शुचयो विपश्चितोऽभि स्तोमैरनूषत
lines_iast: imā u tvā purūvaso giro vardhantu yā mama
pāvakavarṇāḥ śucayo vipaścito'bhi stomairanūṣata

hindi: वे अत्यन्त मधुर वाणियाँ और स्तोत्र ऊपर उठते हैं; सदा विजयी, धन जीतने वाले, अक्षय सहायता वाले, पुरस्कार चाहने वाले रथों की तरह।
english: Those sweetest songs and hymns rise up, ever-victorious, winning wealth, of unfailing help, like chariots striving for the prize.

text_flags.why: possible: visarga missing before the following s of stomāsa; read as giraḥ

notes: The agreement of line 2 (nominative plural adjectives) with stomāsaḥ/giraḥ is taken as 'the hymns, like chariots'; the sense of the simile is literal.
lines_deva: उदु त्ये मधुमत्तमा गिर स्तोमास ईरते
सत्राजितो धनसा अक्षितोतयो वाजयन्तो रथा इव
lines_iast: udu tye madhumattamā gira stomāsa īrate
satrājito dhanasā akṣitotayo vājayanto rathā iva

hindi: जैसे प्यासा जंगली बैल जल से बने स्थान, बंजर भूमि की ओर जाता है, वैसे ही हमारे निकट आने और बढ़ने पर शीघ्र आओ; कण्वों के बीच साथ मिलकर अच्छी तरह पियो।
english: As a thirsty wild bull goes to the place made by the waters [the barren ground], so come quickly to us in our approach and advance; drink well together among the Kaṇvas.
notes: apā kṛtam, averiṇam, āpitve and prapitve are uncertain; rendered literally. averiṇam read as ava-iriṇam or a variant of iriṇa 'barren ground, salt-lick'; no firm reading. kaṇveṣu 'among the Kaṇvas' (the sage family) is a proper name.
lines_deva: यथा गौरो अपा कृतं तृष्यन्नेत्यवेरिणम्
आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमा गहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब
lines_iast: yathā gauro apā kṛtaṃ tṛṣyannetyaveriṇam
āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamā gahi kaṇveṣu su sacā piba

hindi: हे शक्तियों के स्वामी इन्द्र, सब सहायताओं से भली-भाँति सहायता करो; क्योंकि हे शूर, हम तुम्हारे पीछे चलते हैं, जो यशस्वी और धन पाने वाले हो, जैसे भग के पीछे।
english: Help us well, O lord of powers, Indra, with all your aids; for we follow you, O hero, the glorious finder of wealth, as one follows Bhaga.
notes: The 3 in śagdhyū3ṣu is the pluta mark (prolongation) on ū. The comparison 'bhagaṃ na' is taken as 'like Bhaga', Bhaga being the bestower of fortune.
lines_deva: शग्ध्यू३षु शचीपत इन्द्र विश्वाभिरूतिभिः
भगं न हि त्वा यशसं वसुविदमनु शूर चरामसि
lines_iast: śagdhyū3ṣu śacīpata indra viśvābhirūtibhiḥ
bhagaṃ na hi tvā yaśasaṃ vasuvidamanu śūra carāmasi

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सूर्य का प्रकाश पाने वाले तुमने असुरों से जो भोग लाए, हे मघवन्, इस स्तोता को बढ़ाओ और जिन्होंने तुममें कुश बिछाया है, उन्हें भी।
english: O Indra, winner of the light of heaven, [with] the enjoyments that you brought from the Asuras, make this singer grow, O bountiful one, and those who have strewn the sacred grass for you.
notes: yā is read as yāḥ (acc. pl. f. relative agreeing with bhujaḥ). asya vardhaya: 'make grow' with asya ('of this') is uncertain; read as 'this (singer)'. svarvān follows the glossary: svar = light of heaven.
lines_deva: या इन्द्र भुज आभरः स्वर्वाँ असुरेभ्यः
स्तोतारमिन्मघवन्नस्य वर्धय ये च त्वे वृक्तबर्हिषः
lines_iast: yā indra bhuja ābharaḥ svarvā~ asurebhyaḥ
stotāraminmaghavannasya vardhaya ye ca tve vṛktabarhiṣaḥ

hindi: मित्र और अर्यमा के लिए संगति योग्य स्तोत्र गाओ, हे सत्यधन वाले; रक्षक वरुण के लिए मनभावन वचन और स्तुति-गान राजाओं में गाओ।
english: Sing forth to Mitra and to Aryaman a song fit for fellowship, O rich in truth; sing to Varuṇa the protector a pleasing word, a song of praise, among the kings.
notes: ṛtāvaso is read as a vocative 'O rich in truth' (uncertain; addressee unclear). varūthye3 is taken as a locative agreeing with varuṇe with a pluta mark (e3); the Rigveda has varūthyam (acc.) agreeing with vacaḥ, so the Sāmaveda form is a variant and the reading is uncertain. The addressed 'kings' are Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. Reviewer: the identification of the 'kings' with Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman is an interpretation, not stated in the text.
lines_deva: प्र मित्राय प्रार्यम्णे सचथ्यमृतावसो
वरूथ्ये३ वरुणे छन्द्यं वचः स्तोत्रँ राजसु गायत
lines_iast: pra mitrāya prāryamṇe sacathyamṛtāvaso
varūthye3 varuṇe chandyaṃ vacaḥ stotra~ rājasu gāyata

hindi: हे इन्द्र, पहले पीने के लिए मनुष्य स्तोत्रों से तुम्हारी ओर आते हैं। संगठित ऋभुओं ने मिलकर गाया; रुद्र तुम प्राचीन की स्तुति करते हैं।
english: Men [come] to you with hymns, O Indra, for the first drinking. The united Ṛbhus sang together; the Rudras praise you, the ancient one.
notes: abhi is taken with an understood verb ('approach / praise'). Whether pūrvyam is Indra (taken here) or a thing praised is not certain.
lines_deva: अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इन्द्र स्तोमेभिरायवः
समीचीनास ऋभवः समस्वरन्रुद्रा गृणन्त पूर्व्यम्
lines_iast: abhi tvā pūrvapītaya indra stomebhirāyavaḥ
samīcīnāsa ṛbhavaḥ samasvaranrudrā gṛṇanta pūrvyam

hindi: हे मरुतो, महान इन्द्र के लिए प्रार्थना-स्तोत्र उठाओ। वृत्रहन्ता, सौ शक्तियों वाला सौ गाँठों वाले वज्र से वृत्र को मारता है।
english: O Maruts, raise a prayer to great Indra. The slayer of Vṛtra, of a hundred powers, slays Vṛtra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
notes: vaḥ is rendered 'for you' (dative of interest). Vṛtra is treated as a name. Reviewer: vaḥ is not rendered separately in the translations (the address is carried by 'O Maruts').
lines_deva: प्र व इन्द्राय बृहते मरुतो ब्रह्मार्चत
वृत्रँ हनति वृत्रहा शतक्रतुर्वज्रेण शतपर्वणा
lines_iast: pra va indrāya bṛhate maruto brahmārcata
vṛtra~ hanati vṛtrahā śatakraturvajreṇa śataparvaṇā

words.gram: n. acc. sg. superl. (agrees with bṛhat)

hindi: हे मरुतो, इन्द्र के लिए वृत्र का सर्वश्रेष्ठ संहार करने वाले बृहत् साम को गाओ, जिससे सत्य को बढ़ाने वालों ने ज्योति उत्पन्न की; देव के लिए दिव्य, जागरूक गान।
english: Sing to Indra, O Maruts, the great chant (Bṛhat), the best slayer of Vṛtra, by which those who strengthen truth brought forth light: a divine, wakeful [song] for the god.
notes: bṛhat may be the name of the chant (Bṛhat sāman) or simply 'great (song)'; devam jāgṛvi is taken as 'divine, wakeful (song)' for the god.
lines_deva: बृहदिन्द्राय गायत मरुतो वृत्रहन्तमम्
येन ज्योतिरजनयन्नृतावृधो देवं देवाय जागृवि
lines_iast: bṛhadindrāya gāyata maruto vṛtrahantamam
yena jyotirajanayannṛtāvṛdho devaṃ devāya jāgṛvi

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जैसे पिता पुत्रों के लिए, वैसे हमारे लिए बुद्धि-कौशल लाओ। हे बहुतों से पुकारे गए, इस यात्रा में हमारी सहायता करो, कि हम जीवित रहते हुए प्रकाश पाएँ।
english: O Indra, bring us insight, as a father does for his sons. Help us, O much-invoked one, on this course, so that we may attain the light while living.
notes: śikṣā is the Vedic lengthened form of śikṣa; ṇo is naḥ.
lines_deva: इन्द्र क्रतुं न आ भर पिता पुत्रेभ्यो यथा
शिक्षा णो अस्मिन्पुरुहूत यामनि जीवा ज्योतिरशीमहि
lines_iast: indra kratuṃ na ā bhara pitā putrebhyo yathā
śikṣā ṇo asminpuruhūta yāmani jīvā jyotiraśīmahi

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हमें मत छोड़ो; हमारे साझे आनन्द-भोज में हमारे साथ रहो। तुम हमारी सहायता हो, तुम्हीं हमारे बन्धु हो; हे इन्द्र, हमें मत छोड़ो।
english: Do not forsake us, O Indra; be with us at the common feast. You are our help, you alone are our kinship; do not forsake us, O Indra.
notes: ūtī is read as 'help' (nominative; an instrumental 'by aid' is also possible). sadhamādye 'at the common feast' is a locative. bhavā is bhava with Vedic lengthening; vṛṇag is vṛṇak with voicing before bh.
lines_deva: मा न इन्द्र परा वृणग्भवा नः सधमाद्ये
त्वं न ऊती त्वमिन्न आप्यम् मा न इन्द्र परा वृणक्
lines_iast: mā na indra parā vṛṇagbhavā naḥ sadhamādye
tvaṃ na ūtī tvaminna āpyam mā na indra parā vṛṇak

hindi: हम, सोम निचोड़ने वाले और कुश बिछाने वाले, जल की तरह; हे वृत्रहन्, पवित्र छन्ने की धाराओं पर स्तोता तुम्हारे चारों ओर बैठते हैं।
english: We, indeed, having pressed the Soma and strewn the sacred grass for you, like waters; the singers sit around you, O slayer of Vṛtra, at the streams of the filter.
notes: 'like waters' (āpo na) is unclear in function (it may qualify the Soma streams or the worshippers); rendered literally.
lines_deva: वयं घ त्वा सुतावन्त आपो न वृक्तबर्हिषः
पवित्रस्य प्रस्रवणेषु वृत्रहन्परि स्तोतार आसते
lines_iast: vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvanta āpo na vṛktabarhiṣaḥ
pavitrasya prasravaṇeṣu vṛtrahanpari stotāra āsate

hindi: हे इन्द्र, नहुष की प्रजाओं में और जातियों में जो बल और पौरुष है, अथवा पाँचों जनों का जो द्युम्न है, वह सब यहाँ ले आओ, पौरुष के सब कार्य पूरी तरह ले आओ।
english: Whatever strength and manly vigour, O Indra, [is] among the Nahuṣa peoples and the tribes, or whatever splendour [belongs] to the five peoples, bring [it] here, altogether, all manly deeds.
notes: nāhuṣīṣu is read as 'among the Nahuṣa (peoples)'; the ā after it is taken with ā bhara in line 2 (separated prefix). 'for us' is not in the text.
lines_deva: यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वा ओजो नृम्णं च कृष्टिषु
यद्वा पञ्च क्षितीनां द्युम्नमा भर सत्रा विश्वानि पौँस्या
lines_iast: yadindra nāhuṣīṣvā ojo nṛmṇaṃ ca kṛṣṭiṣu
yadvā pañca kṣitīnāṃ dyumnamā bhara satrā viśvāni pau~syā

hindi: सचमुच तुम बैल जैसे बलवान हो, बैल जैसे वेग वाले हमारे रक्षक। हे उग्र, तुम दूर में बलवान सुने जाते हो, और निकट में भी बलवान प्रसिद्ध हो।
english: Truly you are mighty as a bull, our helper of bull-like impulse. For, O fierce one, you are heard of as the bull in the far, and renowned as the bull in the near.
notes: vṛṣan 'bull' is rendered 'mighty as a bull'; vṛṣajūtiḥ 'of bull-like impulse' is a literal bahuvrīhi.
lines_deva: सत्यमित्था वृषेदसि वृषजूतिर्नोऽविता
वृषा ह्युग्र शृण्विषे परावति वृषो अर्वावति श्रुतः
lines_iast: satyamitthā vṛṣedasi vṛṣajūtirno'vitā
vṛṣā hyugra śṛṇviṣe parāvati vṛṣo arvāvati śrutaḥ

hindi: हे शक्र, तुम चाहे दूर हो या निकट, हे वृत्रहन्, वहाँ से भी, हे इन्द्र, सोम निचोड़ने वाला स्तुतियों के साथ और लम्बे केशों वालों के साथ तुम्हें यहाँ मनाता है।
english: Whether you are in the far, O mighty one (Śakra), or in the near, O slayer of Vṛtra, from there the Soma-presser seeks to win you, O Indra, with songs and with the long-maned [horses].
notes: dyugat is uncertain (read as 'heaven-going / heavenly'); the grouping of gīrbhiḥ and keśibhiḥ with vivāsati is also uncertain. vivāsati (desiderative of √vas 'shine'?) is rendered 'seeks to win, propitiates' as an approximation. Reviewer: dyugat is left untranslated in Hindi and English because its construction is unclear.
lines_deva: यच्छक्रासि परावति यदर्वावति वृत्रहन्
अतस्त्वा गीर्भिर्द्युगदिन्द्र केशिभिः सुतावाँ आ विवासति
lines_iast: yacchakrāsi parāvati yadarvāvati vṛtrahan
atastvā gīrbhirdyugadindra keśibhiḥ sutāvā~ ā vivāsati

hindi: तुम्हारे वीर, ज्ञानी के लिए सोमरस के मद में महान वाणी से गाओ; उस प्रसिद्ध, शक्तिशाली इन्द्र को नाम से, जैसे वचन कहता है।
english: Sing to your hero, the wise one, with a great song in the exhilaration of the juice; [sing] Indra by name, the renowned, the powerful, as the word [says].
notes: vaco yathā is unclear ('as the word says / according to the word'). 'to your hero' takes abhi with gāya; the addressee of gāya is the singer or the priests.
lines_deva: अभि वो वीरमन्धसो मदेषु गाय गिरा महा विचेतसम्
इन्द्रं नाम श्रुत्यँ शाकिनं वचो यथा
lines_iast: abhi vo vīramandhaso madeṣu gāya girā mahā vicetasam
indraṃ nāma śrutya~ śākinaṃ vaco yathā

hindi: हे इन्द्र, कल्याण के लिए तिहरा शरण और तिहरा आश्रय दो; उदार जनों को और मुझे आश्रय दो; इनसे अस्त्र को दूर रखो।
english: O Indra, [grant] a threefold refuge, a triple shelter for welfare. Grant shelter to the bountiful ones and to me, and keep the missile away from these.
notes: 'grant' in line 1 is supplied from yaccha. maghavadbhyaḥ 'bountiful ones' are probably the patrons (interpretation).
lines_deva: इन्द्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्रिवरूथँ स्वस्तये
छर्दिर्यच्छ मघवद्भ्यश्च मह्यं च यावया दिद्युमेभ्यः
lines_iast: indra tridhātu śaraṇaṃ trivarūtha~ svastaye
chardiryaccha maghavadbhyaśca mahyaṃ ca yāvayā didyumebhyaḥ

hindi: सूर्य की शरण में आए हुओं की तरह तुम सब इन्द्र (के दानों) में भाग लो; बल से उत्पन्न हुआ (वह) धन देता है; हम अपने भाग की तरह (उसकी ओर) देखते हैं।
english: Like those who resort to the sun, all of you partake of Indra [his gifts]. [He,] born among beings with might, [gives] riches; we look to [him] as to our share.
notes: Hard verse; only a tentative literal sense is given. janimāni and jāto are uncertain, and the verbs of line 2 are supplied.
lines_deva: श्रायन्त इव सूर्यं विश्वेदिन्द्रस्य भक्षत
वसूनि जातो जनिमान्योजसा प्रति भागं न दीधिमः
lines_iast: śrāyanta iva sūryaṃ viśvedindrasya bhakṣata
vasūni jāto janimānyojasā prati bhāgaṃ na dīdhimaḥ

hindi: बिना देवता को माने हुआ दीर्घायु मनुष्य उस अन्न को नहीं पाता; वह जो चितकबरे घोड़ों के साथ चलने वाला है, जो अपना घोड़ा जोतता है, इन्द्र अपने दो लाल-भूरे घोड़ों को जोतता है।
english: A godless, long-lived mortal has not obtained that refreshment; he who goes with dappled steeds, who yokes his steed, [that is] Indra; he yokes his two bay horses.

text_flags.why: possible: cit + yaḥ (ya before e); the long ā is unexplained
possible: 3 sg. middle ending -te, as in the second yuyojate of the same line

notes: Hard verse. etagvā cit yaḥ etaśaḥ yuyojate is read as 'he who goes with dappled steeds, who yokes his Etaśa'; the syntax connecting the two lines is uncertain. dīrghāyo is read as dīrghāyaḥ (stem uncertain).
lines_deva: न सीमदेव आप तदिषं दीर्घायो मर्त्यः
एतग्वा चिद्या एतशो युयोजत इन्द्रो हरी युयोजते
lines_iast: na sīmadeva āpa tadiṣaṃ dīrghāyo martyaḥ
etagvā cidyā etaśo yuyojata indro harī yuyojate

words.gloss: O one equal to the hymn (?)

hindi: हमारे लिए सब युद्धों में पुकारने योग्य इन्द्र का सत्कार करो; हे वृत्रहन्, परम बल वाले, ऋचा के समान, प्रार्थनाओं और सवनों के निकट आओ।
english: Honour Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, for us; [come] near the prayers and pressings, O slayer of Vṛtra, O one of supreme might, O equal to the hymn.
notes: Hard verse. bhūṣata (2 pl.) is taken as 'attend on, honour'; paramajyā and ṛcīṣama are uncertain (ṛcīṣama is an epithet of Indra, 'equal to the hymn / matching the verses'); 'come' in line 2 is supplied.
lines_deva: आ नो विश्वासु हव्यमिन्द्रँ समत्सु भूषत
उप ब्रह्माणि सवनानि वृत्रहन्परमज्या ऋचीषम
lines_iast: ā no viśvāsu havyamindra~ samatsu bhūṣata
upa brahmāṇi savanāni vṛtrahanparamajyā ṛcīṣama

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सबसे निम्न धन तुम्हारा ही है; तुम बीच वाले का पोषण करते हो। तुम सब पर और सबसे ऊँचे पर पूरी तरह शासन करते हो; गौओं के विषय में कोई तुम्हें नहीं रोकता।
english: Yours indeed, O Indra, is the lowest wealth; you nourish the middle [one]. You rule altogether over all and over the highest; no one obstructs you in the matter of cattle.
notes: avamam vasu and madhyamam are read as 'lowest wealth' and 'the middle [wealth]'; vṛṇvate is taken as 'obstruct, hold back' (alternative 'choose').
lines_deva: तवेदिन्द्रावमं वसु त्वं पुष्यसि मध्यमम्
सत्रा विश्वस्य परमस्य राजसि न किष्ट्वा गोषु वृण्वते
lines_iast: tavedindrāvamaṃ vasu tvaṃ puṣyasi madhyamam
satrā viśvasya paramasya rājasi na kiṣṭvā goṣu vṛṇvate

hindi: तुम कहाँ जाते हो? कहाँ हो? तुम्हारा मन तो अनेक स्थानों में है। हे योद्धा, हलचल मचाने वाले, हे पुरन्दर, तुम दौड़ते हो; गायत्र गाने वालों ने गान किया है।
english: Where do you go? Where are you? For your mind is in many places. You hasten, O warrior, maker of tumult, O destroyer of forts; the Gāyatra singers have sung forth.
notes: alarṣi and khajakṛt are uncertain (khaja read as 'tumult, commotion'). gāyatrāḥ is taken as 'singers of Gāyatra verses'.
lines_deva: क्वेयथ क्वेदसि पुरुत्रा चिद्धि ते मनः
अलर्षि युध्म खजकृत्पुरन्दर प्र गायत्रा अगासिषुः
lines_iast: kveyatha kvedasi purutrā ciddhi te manaḥ
alarṣi yudhma khajakṛtpurandara pra gāyatrā agāsiṣuḥ

words.gram: 2 sg. impv. √bhṛ (bharā with lengthening; a plural bharata would be expected beside bhūṣata)
m. dat. sg. or loc. sg. (uncertain)

hindi: हम आज और कल यहाँ इस वज्रधारी को तृप्त करते आए हैं; उसके लिए आज सवन में निचोड़ा हुआ सोम लाओ और अब उस प्रसिद्ध का सत्कार करो।
english: Today and yesterday we have strengthened him here, the wielder of the thunderbolt; bring the pressed Soma to him today at the pressing, and now honour the renowned one.
notes: hyopīpemeha is read hyaḥ apīpema iha. bharā read as bhara (Vedic lengthening; 2 pl.). śrute is uncertain (dative/locative 'to the renowned one').
lines_deva: वयमेनमिदा ह्योपीपेमेह वज्रिणम्
तस्मा उ अद्य सवने सुतं भरा नूनं भूषत श्रुते
lines_iast: vayamenamidā hyopīpemeha vajriṇam
tasmā u adya savane sutaṃ bharā nūnaṃ bhūṣata śrute

hindi: जो प्रजाओं का राजा है, रथों पर चलने वाला, अदम्य है, सब सेनाओं को पार करने वाला, जो सबसे श्रेष्ठ वृत्रहन्ता है, उसकी मैं स्तुति करता हूँ।
english: He who is king of the peoples, who goes in chariots, irresistible, the overcomer of all hosts, the foremost, who is the slayer of Vṛtra: I praise [him].
notes: jyeṣṭham (foremost) is taken as the object of gṛṇe with the relative clauses; 'him' is supplied.
lines_deva: यो राजा चर्षणीनां याता रथेभिरध्रिगुः
विश्वासां तरुता पृतनानां ज्येष्ठं यो वृत्रहा गृणे
lines_iast: yo rājā carṣaṇīnāṃ yātā rathebhiradhriguḥ
viśvāsāṃ tarutā pṛtanānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ yo vṛtrahā gṛṇe

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जिससे हम डरते हैं, उससे हमें अभय करो। हे मघवन्, सहायता करो; तुम्हारा वह हमारी रक्षा के लिए है; शत्रुओं को दूर मारो, आक्रमणकारियों को दूर मारो।
english: From whatever we fear, O Indra, make safety for us from that. O bountiful one, help; that [power] of yours is for our protection. Strike away the enemies, strike away the foes.
notes: tava tan na ūtaye is read as 'that [power/help] of yours is for our protection' (the noun is supplied).
lines_deva: यत इन्द्र भयामहे ततो नो अभयं कृधि
मघवञ्छग्धि तव तन्न ऊतये वि द्विषो वि मृधो जहि
lines_iast: yata indra bhayāmahe tato no abhayaṃ kṛdhi
maghavañchagdhi tava tanna ūtaye vi dviṣo vi mṛdho jahi

hindi: हे घर के स्वामी, दृढ़ स्तम्भ, सोम के योग्य जनों का सत्र; प्राचीन पुरों का भेदने वाला, बूँद, इन्द्र, मुनियों का मित्र।
english: O lord of the dwelling, firm pillar, the session of the Soma-worthy ones; the drop, breaker of the ancient forts, Indra, friend of the sages.
notes: Hard verse. dhruvā sthūṇām, satram and drapsaḥ are uncertain; the line seems to be a string of epithets of Indra with no verb. 'sthūṇā~' is read as sthūṇām (candrabindu before s). Reviewer: dhruvā (f. nom./instr.) and sthūṇām (f. acc.) do not agree in case, so 'firm pillar' is tentative; the line may be corrupt.
lines_deva: वास्तोष्पते ध्रुवा स्थूणाँ सत्रँ सोम्यानाम्
द्रप्सः पुरां भेत्ता शश्वतीनामिन्द्रो मुनीनाँ सखा
lines_iast: vāstoṣpate dhruvā sthūṇā~ satra~ somyānām
drapsaḥ purāṃ bhettā śaśvatīnāmindro munīnā~ sakhā

hindi: सचमुच, हे सूर्य, तुम महान हो; सचमुच, हे आदित्य, तुम महान हो। तुम जो हो, तुम्हारी महिमा महान है, हे सबसे प्रशंसनीय; हे देव, तुम अपनी महिमा से महान हो।
english: Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great. Great is the greatness of you who are, O most admirable; by greatness, O god, you are great.
notes: baṇ- in baṇmahā~ is baṭ with nasal assimilation before m. mahaste sato is read mahaḥ te sataḥ.
lines_deva: बण्महाँ असि सूर्य बडादित्य महाँ असि
महस्ते सतो महिमा पनिष्टम मह्ना देव महाँ असि
lines_iast: baṇmahā~ asi sūrya baḍāditya mahā~ asi
mahaste sato mahimā paniṣṭama mahnā deva mahā~ asi

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारा जो मित्र है, वह घोड़ों, रथ, सुन्दर रूप और गायों वाला है; वह सदा बल-आयु से युक्त रहता है और चमकती वस्तुओं के साथ सभा में जाता है।
english: He who is your friend, O Indra, has horses, a chariot, a fair form and cattle; he is always accompanied by vigorous life, and goes to the assembly with shining [things].
notes: śvātrabhājā is uncertain (śvātra read as 'vigour, quickness'; the form agrees with vayasā). candraiḥ 'with shining (ornaments, gold)' is a tentative rendering.
lines_deva: अश्वी रथी सुरूप इद्गोमाँ यदिन्द्र ते सखा
श्वात्रभाजा वयसा सचते सदा चन्द्रैर्याति सभामुप
lines_iast: aśvī rathī surūpa idgomā~ yadindra te sakhā
śvātrabhājā vayasā sacate sadā candrairyāti sabhāmupa

hindi: हे इन्द्र, यदि तुम्हारे लिए सौ द्यौ और सौ भूमियाँ हों, तो भी, हे वज्रधारी, हज़ार सूर्य भी तुम्हारे बराबर नहीं हैं; उत्पन्न हुए दोनों लोक भी तुम्हें नहीं पा सके।
english: Even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths for you, O Indra, a thousand suns would not match you, O wielder of the thunderbolt; nor have the two worlds, once born, reached you.
notes: anu with na is read as 'would not match / follow'; aṣṭa is read as 3 sg. aorist of √aś 'reach'. śata~ is śatam (candrabindu before s).
lines_deva: यद्द्याव इन्द्र ते शतँ शतं भूमीरुत स्युः
न त्वा वज्रिन्त्सहस्रँ सूर्या अनु न जातमष्ट रोदसी
lines_iast: yaddyāva indra te śata~ śataṃ bhūmīruta syuḥ
na tvā vajrintsahasra~ sūryā anu na jātamaṣṭa rodasī

hindi: हे इन्द्र, चाहे पूर्व, पश्चिम, उत्तर या दक्षिण में मनुष्य तुम्हें पुकारें, तुम सब ओर बहुत स्थानों में मनुष्यों से प्रेरित हो; हे साहसी, तुम आनव में हो, तुर्वश में हो।
english: Whether you are invoked by men in the east, west, north or south, O Indra, you are everywhere, in many places, urged on by men; you are among the Ānavas, O bold one, among the Turvaśas.
notes: The four directions prāk/apāk/udak/nyak are read as east/west/north/south as is usual, with the literal sense 'forward/backward/upward/downward' also possible. simā is read sīm ā (uncertain). Ānava and Turvaśa are tribal names.
lines_deva: यदिन्द्र प्रागपागुदग्न्यग्वा हूयसे नृभिः
सिमा पुरू नृषूतो अस्यानवेऽसि प्रशर्ध तुर्वशे
lines_iast: yadindra prāgapāgudagnyagvā hūyase nṛbhiḥ
simā purū nṛṣūto asyānave'si praśardha turvaśe

words.gloss: wealth, one whose wealth you are

hindi: हे इन्द्र, कौन मनुष्य उसपर आक्रमण करने का साहस करता है जिसके धन तुम हो? हे मघवन्, निर्णायक दिन में, श्रद्धा से पुरस्कार चाहने वाला पुरस्कार पाना चाहता है।
english: O Indra, what mortal dares [attack] him whose wealth you are? For with faith in you, O bountiful one, on the decisive day the prize-seeker strives to win the prize.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda has tvāvasum 'having you as wealth' plus ā; the printed split 'tvā vasavā' looks like a corruption

notes: The two tokens tvā, vasavā are read as tvā-vasum ā by comparison with the Rigveda, but this is a suggestion only. pārye divi is uncertain ('decisive day'); śraddhā hi te is taken as 'with faith in you'.
lines_deva: कस्तमिन्द्र त्वा वसवा मर्त्यो दधर्षति
श्रद्धा हि ते मघवन्पार्ये दिवि वाजी वाजँ सिषासति
lines_iast: kastamindra tvā vasavā martyo dadharṣati
śraddhā hi te maghavanpārye divi vājī vāja~ siṣāsati

hindi: हे इन्द्र और अग्नि, यह बिना पैरों वाली पैरों वालियों से पहले आ गई है; सिर को छोड़कर, जीभ से पुकारती, चलती हुई उसने तीस पग रखे।
english: O Indra and Agni, this footless one has come before the footed ones; leaving the head, crying with the tongue, moving, she has stepped thirty steps.
notes: A riddle verse; the subject is not named in the text (traditionally dawn, not stated here). pūrvā agāt is read as 'she has come first'.
lines_deva: इन्द्राग्नी अपादियं पूर्वागात्पद्वतीभ्यः
हित्वा शिरो जिह्वया रारपच्चरत्त्रिँशत्पदा न्यक्रमीत्
lines_iast: indrāgnī apādiyaṃ pūrvāgātpadvatībhyaḥ
hitvā śiro jihvayā rārapaccarattri~śatpadā nyakramīt

hindi: हे इन्द्र, निकट आओ, नपी-तुली बुद्धि वाली सहायताओं के साथ; हे अत्यन्त कल्याणकारी, अत्यन्त कल्याणकारी सहायताओं के साथ आओ; हे अच्छे मित्र, अच्छे मित्रों के साथ आओ।
english: Come nearer, O Indra, with aids of measured wisdom; come, O most beneficent one, with most beneficent succours; come, O good friend, with good friends.
notes: The words śaṃ + tama and śaṃ + tamābhiḥ are printed apart but are the compounds śaṃtama 'most beneficent' (voc.) and śaṃtamābhiḥ. mitamedhābhiḥ 'of measured wisdom' is uncertain.
lines_deva: इन्द्र नेदीय एदिहि मितमेधाभिरूतिभिः
आ शं तम शं तमाभिरभिष्टिभिरा स्वापे स्वापिभिः
lines_iast: indra nedīya edihi mitamedhābhirūtibhiḥ
ā śaṃ tama śaṃ tamābhirabhiṣṭibhirā svāpe svāpibhiḥ

hindi: यहाँ से सहायता के साथ तुम्हारे लिए अजर, प्रेरक, किसी से अप्रेरित, तेज़, विजेता, प्रेरित करने वाले, श्रेष्ठ रथी, अपराजित, तुग्रिय में बढ़ने वाले को बुलाओ।
english: From here, with help, [call] for yourselves the ageless one, the impeller, the unimpelled, the swift, the victor, the urger, the best of charioteers, the unconquered one, who grows in the Tugrya (meaning uncertain).
notes: GROUPING: the unit has no finite verb (a list of epithets in the accusative); the sentence probably continues from or into the neighbouring verses. tugriyāvṛdham is uncertain ('growing in the Tugrya / strengthening Tugra's [people]'); the verb 'call' is supplied.
lines_deva: इत ऊती वो अजरं प्रहेतारमप्रहितम्
आशुं जेतारँ हेतारँ रथीतममतूर्तं तुग्रियावृधम्
lines_iast: ita ūtī vo ajaraṃ prahetāramaprahitam
āśuṃ jetāra~ hetāra~ rathītamamatūrtaṃ tugriyāvṛdham

hindi: तुम्हें हमसे दूर कहीं पुरोहित भी न रोक रखें; दूर से या यहाँ पास होकर हमारे साझे आनन्द-भोज में आओ और सुनो।
english: Let not even the priests keep you far from us. Come to our common feast, whether from afar or here, and, being near, listen.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda reading is 'vāghataś canāre asmat'; the printed split 'ca nāre' looks like a mis-division of cana + āre

notes: The jussive mā … rīraman is rendered 'Let not … keep'. vāghataḥ is taken as 'priests / sacrificers'. The end of line 2 is read vā san upa śrudhi ('or being near, listen'); the printed śrudhi corresponds to śṛṇudhi.
lines_deva: मो षु त्वा वाघतश्च नारे अस्मन्नि रीरमन्
आरात्ताद्वा सधमादं न आ गहीह वा सन्नुप श्रुधि
lines_iast: mo ṣu tvā vāghataśca nāre asmanni rīraman
ārāttādvā sadhamādaṃ na ā gahīha vā sannupa śrudhi

words.gloss: to the wielder of the thunderbolt

hindi: सोमपायी वज्रधारी इन्द्र के लिए सोम निचोड़ो; उसकी कृपा के लिए पकाई हुई वस्तुएँ पकाओ; अवश्य करो; उदार देने वाला ही उदार को सुख देता है।
english: Press Soma for Indra, the Soma-drinker, the wielder of the thunderbolt; cook the cooked offerings for his favour; do so indeed. The generous one indeed [gives] happiness to the generous one.
notes: 'do it' (kṛṇudhvam it) is a literal rendering with an unstated object. pṛṇan it pṛṇate mayaḥ is taken as 'the generous giver [gives] happiness to the one who gives'; its application (Indra / the patron) is not stated in the text.
lines_deva: सुनोत सोमपाव्ने सोममिन्द्राय वज्रिणे
पचता पक्तीरवसे कृणुध्वमित्पृणन्नित्पृणते मयः
lines_iast: sunota somapāvne somamindrāya vajriṇe
pacatā paktīravase kṛṇudhvamitpṛṇannitpṛṇate mayaḥ

hindi: जो सर्वविजयी और सबको देखने वाला इन्द्र है, उसे हम पुकारते हैं। हे सहस्र उत्साह वाले, हे महान पौरुष वाले, हे सज्जनों के स्वामी, युद्धों में हमारी वृद्धि के लिए हो जाओ।
english: Him who is all-conquering and all-surveying, Indra, we call. O thousand-spirited one, O one of great manliness, O lord of the good, be in battles for our increase.
notes: sahasramanyo is read as 'of a thousand spirits / wraths'; manyu has both senses, so 'spirited' is a neutral rendering. bhavā is bhava with Vedic lengthening.
lines_deva: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिन्द्रं तँ हूमहे वयम्
सहस्रमन्यो तुविनृम्ण सत्पते भवा समत्सु नो वृधे
lines_iast: yaḥ satrāhā vicarṣaṇirindraṃ ta~ hūmahe vayam
sahasramanyo tuvinṛmṇa satpate bhavā samatsu no vṛdhe

words.gloss: O you two rich in power

hindi: हे शक्ति के धनी दोनों, अपनी शक्तियों से दिन-रात हमारी सहायता करो। तुम दोनों का दान कभी न घटे; तुम्हारा दान हमसे कभी दूर न हो।
english: With your powers, O you two rich in power, favour us by day and by night. May your gift never fail; may your gift never [be far] from us.

text_flags.why: possible: the verb is daśasya 'favour, grant'; di- looks like a slip for da-
the particle cana is printed as two tokens ca + na

notes: The particle cana ('ever', with mā/na 'never') is printed as two tokens ca + na in both places; the tokens ca and na are glossed as its two halves. In line 2 the token nāsmadrātiḥ is cana's second half + asmat rātiḥ. The addressees (dual) are not named in the text.
lines_deva: शचीभिर्नः शचीवसू दिवानक्तं दिशस्यतम्
मा वाँ रातिरुप दसत्कदा च नास्मद्रातिः कदा च न
lines_iast: śacībhirnaḥ śacīvasū divānaktaṃ diśasyatam
mā vā~ rātirupa dasatkadā ca nāsmadrātiḥ kadā ca na

hindi: जब कभी कोई मनुष्य स्तोता उदार की स्तुति करे, तब वह प्रेरित वाणी से वरुण की भी वन्दना करे, जो भिन्न-भिन्न व्रतों वालों का धारक है।
english: Whenever a mortal singer praises the bountiful one, then let him praise Varuṇa with an inspired song, the upholder of those of various rites.
notes: The 'bountiful one' (mīḍhvas) is not named in the text. vipā and vivratānām are uncertain ('inspiration'; 'of those of various rites / ordinances'). Reviewer: dharttāraṃ is the old orthography with doubled t after r; read dhartāram.
lines_deva: यदा कदा च मीढुषे स्तोता जरेत मर्त्यः
आदिद्वन्देत वरुणं विपा गिरा धर्त्तारं विव्रतानाम्
lines_iast: yadā kadā ca mīḍhuṣe stotā jareta martyaḥ
ādidvandeta varuṇaṃ vipā girā dharttāraṃ vivratānām

words.gram: m. voc. sg., name (a dative would be medhyātithaye)

hindi: पियो — गायें, रस का मद — इन्द्र के लिए, हे मेध्यातिथि; जो दोनों लाल-भूरे घोड़ों के साथ मिला हुआ है, जो सुनहरा है, वह वज्रधारी इन्द्र सुनहरा है।
english: Drink — the cows [milk ?], the exhilaration of the juice — for Indra, O Medhyātithi; he who is joined with the two bay horses, who is golden, Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt, golden.

text_flags.why: possible: the sense of 'gā andhaso mada' is unclear; gā read as gāḥ (cows / milk); mada may stand for made 'in the exhilaration'

notes: Obscure verse. Line 1 is not translated with certainty: pāhi with gāḥ, andhasaḥ and madaḥ/made, and the dative indrāya medhyātithe (Medhyātithi is a sage's name) are given a tentative reading. Line 2 lists Indra's qualities (sammiślaḥ with the two bay horses; golden; thunderbolt-wielder).
lines_deva: पाहि गा अन्धसो मद इन्द्राय मेध्यातिथे
यः सम्मिश्लो हर्योर्यो हिरण्यय इन्द्रो वज्री हिरण्ययः
lines_iast: pāhi gā andhaso mada indrāya medhyātithe
yaḥ sammiślo haryoryo hiraṇyaya indro vajrī hiraṇyayaḥ

hindi: इन्द्र इस ओर मुड़कर हमारे दोनों को, इस वचन को सुने; वह मघवा, सबसे बलवान, हमारी एकाग्र प्रार्थना से सोम पीने के लिए यहाँ आए।
english: May Indra, turned toward us, hear both of ours, this word; may the bountiful, most mighty one come with [our] concentrated prayer to drink the Soma.
notes: 'both' (ubhayam) is left general (both praise and request is the usual reading, not stated here). satrācyā dhiyā is rendered 'concentrated prayer'. na (naḥ) is taken as 'ours'.
lines_deva: उभयँ शृणवच्च न इन्द्रो अर्वागिदं वचः
सत्राच्या मघवान्त्सोमपीतये धिया शविष्ठ आ गमत्
lines_iast: ubhaya~ śṛṇavacca na indro arvāgidaṃ vacaḥ
satrācyā maghavāntsomapītaye dhiyā śaviṣṭha ā gamat

hindi: हे पत्थर के धारी, बड़े मूल्य के लिए भी तुम्हें दूर नहीं दिया जाता; हज़ार के लिए नहीं, दस हज़ार के लिए नहीं, हे वज्रधारी, सौ के लिए भी नहीं, हे सौ दान वाले।
english: O wielder of the stone, you are not given away even for a great price; not for a thousand, not for ten thousand, O wielder of the thunderbolt, nor for a hundred, O hundred-gifted one.

text_flags.why: possible: dative ayutāya (parallel to sahasrāya, śatāya); -e looks like a slip

notes: mahe ca na is read mahe cana ('not even for a great [price]'). The Rigveda has a different verb (deyām 'may I give'); the Sāmaveda text dīyase is passive ('you are given'). adrivaḥ follows the glossary rendering (wielder of the stone).
lines_deva: महे च न त्वाद्रिवः परा शुल्काय दीयसे
न सहस्राय नायुताये वज्रिवो न शताय शतामघ
lines_iast: mahe ca na tvādrivaḥ parā śulkāya dīyase
na sahasrāya nāyutāye vajrivo na śatāya śatāmagha

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम मेरे लिए पिता से बेहतर हो, और न देने वाले भाई से भी; और हे वसु, मेरी माता और तुम दोनों समान रूप से धन पाने और सफलता के लिए आश्रय देते हो।
english: O Indra, you are better for me than a father and than a brother who does not share; and my mother and you two shelter [me] equally, O good one, for the winning of goods and for bounty.
notes: Line 2 is uncertain: chadayathaḥ is a dual verb ('you two shelter/cover'), with subjects my mother and (implied) Indra; vasutvanāya and rādhase are rendered tentatively. abhuñjataḥ is read as 'not sharing / not providing' (a-√bhuj).
lines_deva: वस्याँ इन्द्रासि मे पितुरुत भ्रातुरभुञ्जतः
माता च मे छदयथः समा वसो वसुत्वनाय राधसे
lines_iast: vasyā~ indrāsi me pituruta bhrāturabhuñjataḥ
mātā ca me chadayathaḥ samā vaso vasutvanāya rādhase
